insight.title: How the Sky Becomes the Earth
insight.subtitle: A quiet look at how the solid world is woven from the invisible air.

sections.text: We often imagine the solid world is built from the ground up. We see a towering oak and assume its strength comes from the soil beneath its roots. But the truth is far more ethereal. Almost every gram of a tree’s massive weight is pulled, quite literally, out of the invisible air around us.

Through a quiet, rhythmic magic, leaves breathe in carbon. They catch golden sunlight and use that energy to weave gas into solid wood. The heavy branches above your head were once drifting ghosts of molecules. Trees are not grown from the earth. They are simply sunlight and atmosphere made visible and strong.

This tells us that the invisible world is more substantial than we realize. Every forest is a captured breath, a physical record of the sky. When you walk through the woods, you are moving through thin air that decided to become something solid. It reminds us that beauty often begins with what we cannot see.
